bundles.notes: The fern passage concerns reversible dehydration in plant cells, not animal development or life-cycle reversal, and explicitly distinguishes dormancy from death.

The axolotl passage explains coordinated tissue repair after injury through wound covering, blastema formation, positional signals, and regrowth; it does not reuse the source organism or lifecycle sequence.

pairDistinctness.notes: A explains survival through dehydration and rehydration in a plant; B explains multi-tissue reconstruction after injury in an animal. Their mechanisms and scientific implications are distinct.
